messages:
anya: Quick sync — we need to lock the v2 compatibility scope before we cut the beta branch. Two high-level options: (A) break-by-default v2 with migration tooling, or (B) compatibility-first with runtime shims. TL;DR: tradeoffs between operational complexity and customer migration pain.

sam: My vote is B (compat-first). We've seen churn when we force breaking changes. But it does increase runtime complexity and test surface.

leo: Agree with Sam re: customer risk. Technical note: adding a full compatibility layer impacts batch/kcache paths. I ran a microbenchmark — compat shim adds ~12% CPU on the hot path if we translate structured-output/ tools on the fly.

maria: Docs concerns: regardless of A or B we need a migration guide, sample diffs, and automated SDK snippets. We should ship a CLI migration helper that can rewrite common call shapes. I can draft a checklist.

jordan: From CS: large customers expect 9-12 months of runway for breaking endpoints. They want an opt-in preview, public migration timelines, and an automated compatibility report for their traffic.

olivia: UX: For structured output changes, users appreciate a compatibility mapping layer that converts new fields to old schema. If we can't guarantee mapping 100%, we need clear fallbacks and error codes.

anya: Proposal (detailed):
1) Launch approach: opt-in v2-beta (customers can call /v2/* but default remains v1).
2) Compatibility mode: runtime flag `compat_mode=legacy` that maps common v2->v1 differences for chat/completions, embeddings, and tool-calling.
3) Migration tooling: CLI + SDK helpers + docs + sample PR diffs.
4) Launch criteria before GA: migration guide, CLI tool, SDK support (JS/Python/Go/Java), canary traffic with <1% error/regression, and perf regression <=15% for compat mode.

sam: Implementation ask: can we scope compat mapping to the top 10 patterns we see in telemetry first? That reduces work and keeps latency overhead constrained.

leo: Yes — we should target the 10 highest-volume shapes and make the mapping extensible. Also recommend a per-key opt-out: accounts can disable compat_mode at API-key level to avoid overhead.

maria: Timeline request: docs needs two drafts: a lightweight migration checklist (for beta) and a full migration guide (for GA). Can we aim for beta-guide in 3 weeks, GA guide in 10 weeks?

jordan: I'll collect customer commitments for the opt-in beta. If enterprises sign up we can prioritize their migration helpers.

olivia: Need UX copy for deprecation notices. Proposed deprecation cadence: announce at GA, 12 months minimum before v1 sunset, with monthly migration metrics emails during that year.

anya: Engineering estimate? Sam / Leo, can you give a rough split for phases?

sam: Phase 0 (design + infra hooks) ~2w. Phase 1 (compat mappings top10 + tests) ~4-6w. Phase 2 (SDKs + CLI + docs + canary) ~3w. Phase 3 (GA hardening + rollout infra) ~4w. So total ~13-15w to GA if we run sequentially; we can parallelize docs + SDKs.

leo: Confirming sam's numbers. Also note we need a perf opt path: offer quantized/compat-enabled model variants to mitigate CPU cost. That adds ops work but is optional.

anya: Draft deprecation timeline I'd like to propose:
- Beta launch (opt-in) in 6 weeks.
- GA in ~15 weeks (if all criteria met).
- v1 deprecation announcement at GA with 12 month sunset.

maria: I'll own the migration guide PRs. Deliverables: beta-checklist (3w), full-guide (10w), SDK examples repo updated at beta.

sam: I'll own server-side compat mappings and rollout plan. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-platform for capacity.

leo: I'll own perf benchmarks and compat-mode opt-out feature.

jordan: I'll coordinate customer signups and create a migration priority list.

olivia: I'll prepare deprecation UX + notification cadence.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: v2-compat-design-doc -> staging at 2026-06-08T10:00Z :rocket:

anya: Action items (short):
- [anya] finalize the scope doc by EOD tomorrow.
- [sam] draft engineering plan + risk list in 2 days.
- [maria] draft beta-checklist in 3w.
- [leo] run perf microbenchmarks and confirm 12% number with different batch sizes.
- [jordan] gather top 5 customers who need extended runway.
- [olivia] draft deprecation copy and email cadence.

sam: +1 to those owners. I'll create a kanban epic and add the 10-pattern tracking ticket.

anya: Thanks all. We'll re-run this thread after Sam posts the engineering plan. If anyone has concerns about the compat-mode per-key opt-out, flag here. :thumbsup:
